Article Title: ‘Rahul Gandhi fostering chaos’: BJP questions Congress over SIR row
Article Text:
Sudhanshu targets Rahul Gandhi over SIR row

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi on Monday accused the Congress and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi of spreading a “false narrative” over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the Opposition was attempting to create confusion and undermine constitutional institutions.Calling Rahul Gandhi the “greatest challenge to India’s democracy”, Trivedi claimed that certain forces, both within and outside the country, were unhappy with India's progress in areas such as artificial intelligence, defence production and national security, and that the Opposition had become a “mere plaything in their hands”.Trivedi also questioned the Congress's allegations over the electoral roll revision process, pointing to the role of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and Booth Level Agents (BLAs). He said the Election Commission had appointed around 12 lakh BLOs across the country, while political parties had appointed approximately 22 lakh BLAs to monitor the process of adding and deleting names from electoral rolls“Were the Congress Party’s BLAs asleep or under the influence of intoxicants? They signed off on these lists or, if they didn’t sign, did they raise any objections?” he asked.The BJP leader argued that political parties had representatives to monitor the revision process and questioned why the Congress was raising objections if its agents had not flagged discrepancies at the time.Trivedi also cited the Congress's electoral performance in several states to counter Rahul Gandhi's claims about anti-incumbency and the party's prospects. He said the Congress had not had a chief minister in Odisha for 25 years, had been out of power in Gujarat since 1995, and in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar since 1990.“These states account for 120 seats,” he said, adding that the Congress had struggled to win even 10 seats across states with a combined 230 Lok Sabha constituencies. He questioned how the party expected to reach the 272-seat majority mark under these circumstances.Trivedi further referred to Kerala, where the Congress's political opponents are in power, and cited state leader Ramesh Chennithala's reported remarks that they had benefited from the SIR exercise. He used this to question the Opposition's criticism of the revision process.His remarks come amid the Opposition's intensified campaign against the SIR exercise. On Sunday, November 1, INDIA bloc leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav and Farooq Abdullah, held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan under the banner of 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao'.The rally followed a march from Minto Road towards the venue, with Opposition leaders accusing the Election Commission of large-scale voter deletions and demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In another X post, Union home minister Amit Shah also targetted Congress."Facing repeated rejections in elections, Congress is now hell-bent on grabbing power by destroying democracy through anarchy. Citizens have braced themselves to shield our democracy from these attacks. This evening, will join the Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy march in Hyderabad," he wrote .
Article Summary: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi accuses Rahul Gandhi of spreading a ‘false narrative’ over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He claims the Opposition was attempting to create confusion and undermine constitutional institutions.

Article Title: 2 Congress workers held for hurling beer bottles at BJP headquarters in Kerala
Article Text:
In a heated political climate in Thiruvananthapuram, two Congress party workers were apprehended for allegedly hurling beer bottles at the BJP headquarters in Kerala.

Two Congress workers were arrested on Monday for allegedly throwing beer bottles at the BJP's Kerala state headquarters, Mararji Bhavan, in Thiruvananthapuram around a month ago, police said.The arrested individuals have been identified as Sujith Kumar and Arun, both associated with local Congress units, according to the news agency PTI.According to police, the incident occurred amid heightened tensions between rival political groups following a series of clashes involving different political outfits in Thiruvananthapuram district.The situation had worsened after Youth Congress workers waved black flags at the convoy of Union Home Minister Amit Shah during the last week of September. Article Title: 1984 survivors, Sikh groups question timing of INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, seek apology
Article Text:
Sikh riot survivors and BJP leaders protest Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on the 42nd anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Survivors of the 1984 anti-Sikh killings and Sikh organisations Sunday questioned Congress's decision to hold the INDIA bloc rally on Nov 1, the 42nd anniversary of the massacre. With Punjab assembly elections due in 2027, the rally's timing also gave BJP political ammunition against Congress.The day saw a BJP-organised protest march in West Delhi, objections from victims' groups and renewed demands for justice.In West Delhi, Sikh community members and survivors joined a march from Hari Nagar towards Tilak Nagar, demanding an apology from Congress and Rahul Gandhi. Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa and senior advocate HS Phoolka, who has represented riot victims for decades, participated."Nov 1 is not only a black day for the Sikhs but the entire country. They (Congress) should also observe it as a black day and hang their heads in shame," Phoolka had said ahead of the rally.The 1984 Riot Victims Welfare Society also objected to the timing of the rally. Its representatives, who had met Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Friday, said Nov 1 was a day of mourning, not political mobilisation. They also raised pending demands for housing, employment and rehabilitation.Society president Surjit Singh sought dignified rehabilitation, while women's wing president Bibi Gurdeep Kaur recalled losing eight family members in the violence.Rajya Sabha MP Vikramjit Singh Sahney, who met survivors in Delhi, recalled losing four family members and alleged that the killings were systematically planned.Separately, SGPC president Harjinder Singh Dhami described the massacre as "a stain on the forehead of the world's largest democracy". "Until those responsible are punished for their actions, the hearts of the victim families will not find peace," he said.
Article Summary: Riot Victims Welfare Society also objected to the timing of the rally. Its representatives said Nov 1 was a day of mourning, not political mobilisation. Sikh community members and survivors joined a march from Hari Nagar towards Tilak Nagar, demanding an apology from Congress.

Article Title: Gyanesh has to go, PM & Shah next, says Rahul Gandhi at anti-CEC rally
Article Text:
Around 50,000 people turned up for INDIA bloc’s rally in Delhi on Sunday, according to Delhi Police estimates

2024 polls illegal, says Rahul; Modi picking voters: Kharge

NEW DELHI: In a Ramlila Maidan packed with protesters and ringing with anti-BJP and anti-CEC slogans Sunday, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said the opposition will confront the top BJP duo of Narendra Modi and Amit Shah after Gyanesh Kumar's removal as chief election commissioner. The trio was losing sleep over the agitation, he claimed, and said the CEC's exit would be the first step in putting the country back on track.With opposition biggies Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, Tejashwi Yadav, Dipankar Bhattacharya, MA Baby, Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti on the dais, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha said the "voice of the people of India" is greater to him than religion, and he will brook no assault on it.Mocking BJP's catchphrase - "Modi kahin nahin jayega" - which was coined in response to Kharge's comment, Rahul said the PM won't be allowed to go anywhere. "You cannot flee... You will stay here and face action."With a “vote bachao, desh bachao” banner forming the backdrop of the dais, the speakers focused on “vote chori”, repeating allegations about SIR and deletion of around 14 crore voters. Rahul accused the CEC, PM and Shah of suppressing the voice of people through “vote chori”.While Mamata and Akhilesh said the West Bengal mandate to BJP was “stolen”, Rahul mentioned the Maharashtra, Haryana, Chhattisgarh, MP and 2024 Lok Sabha polls.He said the 2024 polls were illegal, arguing the difference between NDA and opposition was merely 3%, while 15% of the 2024 voters have been deleted under SIR. “Modi is selecting the voters,” Congress chief Kharge said.Led by Kharge, most INDIA bloc members stressed ejecting BJP from office was a must to save democracy, even leading the crowd in “BJP hatao, desh bachao” chants.Some reminded the crowd that Ramlila Maidan has been the harbinger of history and change in the past. SP chief Akhilesh called the historic venue the “Haldighati of democracy”, referring to the battlefield in Rajasthan where Maharana Pratap faced off with the Mughals in 1576, remembered as a symbol of defiant resistance to a powerful empire.Addressing the crowd that had been growing since 9am and remained eager even as main INDIA bloc members came on the dais only by 3pm, Akhilesh, who occupied a key spot with UP polls looming, hit out at Modi, saying, “Jo UP se aaye the, woh UP se hi jaayenge (those who came from UP, will go from UP)”.“The UP poll results will see off BJP from office in Lucknow and Delhi,” he said, also raising “chanda chori” in Ayodhya in his speech. Akhilesh warned BJP was constantly trying to steal elections, even blaming SP’s 2022 assembly defeat on voter list manipulation. The SP chief said UP BJP has stated that 1.27 crore votes of Hindus have been deleted in UP. He said the statement seems designed to “put the blame for their upcoming defeat on someone else” – touching upon the much-talked about “Delhi vs Lucknow” faultlines in BJP. Indulging the sloganeering crowd, Rahul said his predictions always come true, and he was now forecasting that CEC Kumar would go to jail.“Vote chori” is no smalltime shoplifting but a “rarest of rare case” which qualifies as “treason”, Rahul said. “Without Gyanesh, Modi would not be PM and Shah would not be HM. He also accused RSS of capturing all institutions, including judiciary and bureaucracy, while “two or three people like Ambani and Adani have cornered all the wealth”.He said RSSBJP have spread hatred in the country and the opposition wants to restore “mohabbat ki dukaan” and a culture of nonviolence.“...The voice of every citizen of India is more important to me...” he said. NC’s Abdullah said BJPRSS call Muslims Pakistanis, but Muslims have worked to strengthen the country. PDP’s Mehbooba said BJP has destroyed J&K, but it should not be allowed to ruin the country
Article Summary: Around 50,000 people turn up for INDIA bloc’s rally in Delhi on Sunday, according to Delhi Police estimates. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, Tejashwi Yadav and Dipankar Bhattacharya on dais.

Article Title: ‘Nobody can touch this Kumaraswamy’: Union minister dares cops, Karnataka govt over sting row
Article Text:
'Tomorrow, I will give you complete details about how the investigation is being conducted,' Kumaraswamy said

NEW DELHI: The mobile phone allegedly used in the sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah was purchased in New Delhi and subsequently handed over at the official residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy , Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said on Sunday. Responding to the police claims, Kumaraswamy challenged the commissioner and said he would disclose details of the investigation on Monday.According to Singh, the phone was purchased from a shop in Delhi's Karol Bagh by accused Ritesh Pandey and Vinod Sharma before being delivered to Prajwal Prasad at Kumaraswamy's official residence. The handover was allegedly made on the instructions of Prasad, who was present at the residence, the commissioner said, citing Pandey's statement to investigators.Pandey, who was arrested in New Delhi on October 24, is the first accused to be apprehended in connection with the case. Police said technical evidence, including details establishing the phone's purchase and delivery location, supported parts of his account. Investigators have also found evidence of financial transactions between Pandey and Prasad, which are being verified.Reacting to the commissioner's statement, Kumaraswamy told ANI, "Who is this police commissioner? Whatever statement was given today by the Police Commissioner, you will get the statement tomorrow from my side.At what stage has the investigation reached? What steps is the Commissioner taking, and whose position is he trying to secure? I will explain everything tomorrow..."He further questioned the state government's handling of the investigation and said, "What is happening in this state under this government? What is the state of governance? I will put all these details before you tomorrow. This government, the chief minister and the officials of this government- nobody can touch this Kumaraswamy. I will challenge them. They are afraid of me. Tomorrow, I will give you complete details about how the investigation is being conducted under this government and whom the government is trying to protect through the investigation"The police commissioner said notices had been issued to both Sharma and Prasad, but neither had responded. Both are currently absconding and have approached the court seeking anticipatory bail. Police intend to oppose their applications and are searching for the two men. Singh said further questioning would help establish their respective roles and provide more details about the alleged operation.The case relates to two videos containing allegations against Siddaramaiah that surfaced on YouTube in September.
Article Summary: The mobile phone allegedly used in the sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah was purchased in New Delhi. It was then handed over at the official residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh said. Responding to the police claims, KumarasWamy challenged the commissioner and said he would disclose details of the investigation on Monday.

Article Title: 'Rahul trying to sideline Priyanka': BJP's big attack after INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally

NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of attempting to sideline his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, alleging that she was deliberately denied an opportunity to speak at the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan.BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari claimed that the developments reflected growing divisions within the Congress, with the Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps competing for influence within the party."Priyanka Vadra, who has served as the General Secretary of the Congress Party and is Rahul Gandhi’s sister, was not allowed to speak today at the Ramlila Ground. Did Rahul Gandhi prevent her from speaking today?" Bhandari said.He further alleged that Priyanka was kept in the background during Saturday's mock parliament exercise, which he described as Rahul Gandhi's relaunch exercise."And not just today, even yesterday during the Mock Parliament, when Rahul Gandhi's relaunch exercise was taking place, Priyanka Vadra's chair was placed in the second row, and she was not allowed to speak there either," he said."The Rahul camp is insecure about the Priyanka camp, and the Priyanka camp is being suppressed," Bhandari alleged, claiming that Rahul Gandhi was more concerned about sidelining his sister than addressing issues concerning the country or the Congress."Rahul Gandhi, who is undergoing his hundredth relaunch, is not talking about the people of the country or about the Congress Party today; instead, he is merely trying to sideline Priyanka Gandhi Vadra," he added."Between Rahul versus Priyanka, the Congress is divided into two factions, and the public is watching this fight while eating popcorn," the BJP spokesperson said.The BJP's attack came as Rahul Gandhi led the INDIA bloc's rally against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Addressing supporters, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha launched a sharp attack on the Election Commission, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah over allegations of 'vote chori'.Gandhi warned that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed from his post and face imprisonment, while asserting that Modi and Shah would also face legal action over the alleged electoral irregularities."After Gyanesh Kumar, we will stand against you," Gandhi said, warning the BJP leadership not to think it could escape accountability.The rally was attended by several INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, among others.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari claimed that the developments reflected growing divisions within the Congress. The Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps competing for influence within the party, he said. The attack came as Rahul Gandhi led the INDIA bloc's rally against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

BJP MP Sambit Patra took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, questioning their claims of a massive turnout and asking where the 10 lakh people they had expected to gather were."Rahul Gandhi is speaking and empty chairs. Congress couldn't even fill full Ramlila Maidan of capacity 50,000. Article Title: ‘Youth-oppressive NDA govt’: Tejashwi accuses Nitish of toppling Mahagathbandhan regime in 2024
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bihar LoP and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav on Monday accused former chief minister Nitish Kumar of derailing the state's recruitment drive by toppling the Mahagathbandhan government in January 2024, alleging that the change in government stalled the broader promise of 10 lakh jobs for the youth.In a post on X, Tejashwi revisited the large-scale recruitment drive held on November 2, 2023, when 1,20,336 appointment letters were distributed at Patna's Gandhi Maidan under the Mahagathbandhan government. He described the event as part of a larger plan to provide permanent government employment to the youth.Tejashwi alleged that Nitish Kumar toppled the "youth-friendly" Mahagathbandhan government in January 2024 and formed a new government with the NDA , which he described as "youth-oppressive". He claimed that several recruitment proposals, including a public health cadre with more than 1.3 lakh posts, were ready but were stalled after the change in government.In January 2024, Nitish Kumar resigned as Bihar chief minister on January 28, ending the Mahagathbandhan government formed in August 2022 with the RJD, Congress and Left parties. His move came amid growing differences within the alliance and the INDIA bloc.Hours after resigning, Nitish returned to the BJP-led NDA and took oath as chief minister again, with the BJP joining the new government. Tejashwi Yadav, who was deputy chief minister in the outgoing government, moved to the Opposition.Recalling the 2020 Bihar assembly election campaign, Tejashwi said he had promised 10 lakh government jobs if the RJD came to power. He claimed Nitish Kumar had dismissed the promise as impossible at the time.Tejashwi said the RJD extended support to Nitish Kumar in 2022 on the condition that the government provide 10 lakh jobs. After the Mahagathbandhan government was formed, he said, recruitment notifications were issued for the first two phases of the teacher recruitment examination, and more than three lakh teachers were appointed through the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC).He further alleged that when young people demanded jobs after the government change, they were met with police action, including lathi charges and water cannons. Protesters were chased and beaten, he claimed.
Article Summary: Bihar LoP and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav accused former chief minister Nitish Kumar of derailing the state's recruitment drive. He alleged that the change in government stalled the broader promise of 10 lakh jobs for the youth.

Article Title: Punjab: AAP to seek cancellation of membership of 2 MLAs after they quit party
Article Text:
Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra

AAP leaders accuse BJP of inducting 'rejected' politicians

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) will approach the Punjab assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of the legislative membership of its MLAs Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra after both leaders resigned from the party, the party said on Monday.AAP said both legislators had already been suspended from the party over alleged anti-party activities. Following their suspension, the two MLAs resigned from the party's primary membership.The development comes a day after Pathanmajra, who represents Sanaur, and Jouramajra, the MLA from Samana in Patiala district, announced their resignations from the AAP. Their exits came shortly after the party released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Neither of their constituencies figured in the list.The two leaders had also criticised the Bhagwant Mann-led government over several issues, including the drug menace, rising state debt, alleged governance failures and unfulfilled promises.Speaking to the media in Chandigarh on Sunday, Jouramajra questioned the government's handling of the drug problem and raised the cases of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was killed in Mansa, and Dalit man Gulzar Singh, who died by suicide in Sangrur.He also criticised the government over its failure to fulfil the promise of providing minimum support price for crops and alleged a shortage of teachers in government schools.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, accused AAP leaders from Delhi of controlling the Punjab government and claimed that state ministers lacked the authority to independently approve even a single file.Reacting to the resignations, Punjab AAP president Aman Arora accused the BJP of attempting to induct leaders who had left or been expelled from other parties.AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal also criticised the BJP, describing it as a 'kabaad di dukaan' (scrap shop) for collecting rejected political faces.Arora said the party had taken action against its own leaders whenever they allegedly acted against Punjab's interests.Meanwhile, speculation has emerged that both legislators could join the BJP. Pathanmajra had said they would join a party that worked in the interest of Punjab, while reports indicated that the two could formally join the BJP in Delhi.Jouramajra had served as a Cabinet minister in the Bhagwant Mann government from January 2023 to September 2024 before being dropped during a reshuffle. Pathanmajra has also faced a rape case registered following a complaint by a woman from Zirakpur. He was arrested in Gwalior in March 2026 after allegedly escaping police custody and was granted regular bail by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in May.
Article Summary: Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra have resigned from the AAP. The two legislators had already been suspended from the party over alleged anti-party activities. Speculation has emerged that both legislators could join the BJP.

No, Papa!"The TMC leader also directly targeted Gyanesh Kumar, using the nickname 'Vanish Kumar' to accuse him of making votes disappear.She alleged that the Election Commission had not only removed votes but also undermined the counting process in the state."Now central... 'Vanish Kumar' Ji (referring mockingly to an official), you didn't just make votes vanish, you made the entire counting process vanish! By centrally hijacking, you removed more than 1 crore votes in our Bengal! Before the votes... we didn't lose, we were made to lose! We will take revenge for this through politics, we will fight through democracy, we will fight!"Mamata also accused the BJP of using the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise to benefit itself. Taking a dig at the name of the exercise, she offered her own interpretation of the acronym and alleged that it was being used to provide political relief to the ruling party."What does SIR mean? Special Incentives... meaning Special Incentive Relief to a political party like the BJP! What haven't they been given? Now EVMs were looted! Democracy was looted! The Constitution was looted! Rights were looted! Now our election counting was looted!"Calling West Bengal a victim of the circumstances surrounding the SIR exercise, Mamata said her party would continue to resist what she described as an attempt to undermine the state's electoral rights."I want to say... Bengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not back down! We will give our lives, we will fight! We will not back down, our Bengal was looted! From Delhi... we will not loot, we will save democracy, we will bring democracy back."She went on to accuse the BJP of looting institutions, places of worship and public resources. Referring to alleged incidents involving temples, mosques and gurdwaras, she questioned whether such actions could continue unchecked."What hasn't been looted? Temples were looted! Ram Janmabhoomi's money was looted! In our Bengal, temple money was looted, temple money was looted! Gurudwaras... they enter Gurudwaras wearing boots! We have never heard of such a thing! Mosques were looted, Waqf property was looted, the Treasury was looted! What wasn't looted? Dignity was looted, democracy was looted, the Constitution was looted! Will things keep going on like this?"Mamata also alleged that the BJP was using police personnel and central agencies for political purposes. Appealing to police officers not to become involved in party activities, she said:"Using the police, you make them do party work, political organization work! Police became their comrade... BJP comrade! The BJP has no other organization! That is why I want to say, police personnel are like our brothers and sisters... Agencies, don't work with BJP!"Taking another swipe at the BJP's slogan of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas', she contrasted it with what she described as the consequences of the party's rule."You used to say—'Development for all', 'Together with all, development for all'! And now people say—'Together with BJP, destruction for all'!"Earlier in her address, Mamata expressed solidarity with the CJP leadership, Gen Z, students and young people, while acknowledging the presence of opposition leaders, lawyers and civil society groups at the rally. She named several opposition leaders and lawyers who had attended the gathering and praised their efforts."...actually, the Leftist party, all are present here, from Mehbooba Mufti to everybody, and the NGOs, and the social team, who are civil society. They are really trying their best. I am congratulating [and extending] my solidarity to CZP leadership and Gen Z, all the students, and the young generation for their solidarity, for their support, for their fighting."She also briefly commented on her Hindi-speaking abilities, saying she would keep her address short to allow other leaders to speak."Just now you heard Akhilesh Ji... those people can speak good Hindi, I cannot. But whatever broken Hindi I can manage to speak... Tejashwi also spoke very well, and Rahul is also going to speak. I will speak very briefly, because others should also be given a chance to speak, right?"
Article Summary: Mamata Banerjee accuses BJP of stealing votes, undermining democracy and denying people's rights. Former West Bengal chief minister mocks CEC by calling him 'Vanish Kumar' Alleges that more than one crore votes had been removed in West Bengal during the election process.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday staunchly criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for holding an INDIA bloc rally in Delhi's Ramlila Gound on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.He said the "jalsa" would reopen painful memories for the victims and their families, accusing the Congress of showing little sensitivity towards the tragedy.Shah made the remarks in Chandigarh while addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore."Rahul Gandhi's November 1 'jalsa' in Delhi will only rub salt in wounds of anti-Sikh riot victims," Shah was quoted as saying by the news agency PTI.The INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' protest at Ramlila Maidan as part of its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Targeting the Congress over the violence, Shah said thousands of Sikhs were killed in Delhi on November 1, 1984. He recalled how families were torn apart, with people burnt alive, children orphaned, women widowed and homes destroyed.“The day the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, they had to hold a rally,” Shah said, criticising the INDIA bloc for choosing the date for its protest.He also referred to a statement made by then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi after the killings, saying he had watched it on television and could never forget it."And the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi gave a statement and I saw that on TV and I cannot forget that for rest of my life. He had said when a big tree falls, the earth shakes," he said.Shah added that only Congress leaders could make such a remark after thousands of Sikhs had been killed. He also said the Modi government reopened cases linked to the 1984 riots after coming to power in 2014, provided compensation of Rs 5 lakh to the next of kin of each victim and jailed prominent Congress leaders.“India has never witnessed, nor will it ever witness, riots of this kind, incited by a political party,” Shah said.Shah also targeted Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's symbolic proceedings against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. On Saturday, opposition parties had held a mock 'public impeachment' of the poll panel chief, accusing him of facilitating electoral irregularities and demanding action against him.Taking a swipe at Gandhi's political ambitions, Shah said the Congress leader should continue holding mock Parliament sessions if he wanted to become Prime Minister."If you want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life. Your turn won't come," Shah said.He also referred to Gandhi's electoral defeats and took a dig at Sonia Gandhi's reported ambition to see her son become Prime Minister.Shah accused the opposition of disrupting Parliament, spreading falsehoods and creating disorder. He said such conduct would keep the INDIA bloc out of power.“Telling lies, spreading anarchy, not letting Parliament function, this is your 'fitrat' (true nature),” Shah said of the opposition.He also described Rahul Gandhi's 'mohabbat ki dukaan' slogan as a message of hatred, arguing that holding the rally on the anniversary of the 1984 riots showed a lack of sensitivity towards the victims.
Article Summary: Shah invokes memories of 1984 riots. 'Stay in mock Parliament if you want to be PM,' he says. He also refers to Gandhi's electoral defeats and takes a dig at Sonia Gandhi's reported ambition to see her son become Prime Minister. Shah said the Modi government reopened cases linked to the 1984 riots after coming to power in 2014.

Article Title: 'Why do you challenge democracy?' BJP chief Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of acting on behest of foreign powers

NEW DELHI: BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of acting at the behest of foreign powers, alleging that the opposition was attempting to create instability and challenge an elected government under the pretext of defending democracy.Addressing the BJP's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) march in Haryana ’s Rohtak, Nabin said the party's campaign was aimed at countering what he described as a deliberate attempt to spread chaos across the country.Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary was also present on the stage.“As we participate in this 'Save Democracy' march, we must address the atmosphere of chaos and instability that is being deliberately spread throughout the nation,” Nabin said.He alleged that Rahul Gandhi was working to further the agendas of foreign powers and seeking to challenge India's democratic system at their direction.“They are the same purveyors of chaos who have recently been sowing discord abroad. Their associates, members of the Communist Party and certain Congress leaders, talk about 'changing the regime.' But this is a government formed by the mandate of the people; no one can even lay a finger on it,” he said.Nabin also questioned the Congress's criticism of electoral outcomes, arguing that the party accepted democratic mandates when it won elections but raised concerns over the electoral process when it lost.“You (Congress) have no faith in the country’s 1.4 billion people. In whom, then, do you place your trust? In 3 crore infiltrators! I ask you, Rahul Gandhi: what exactly is your intention? Why do you challenge democracy?” he said.Citing electoral outcomes in different states, Nabin said the Congress described democracy as having prevailed when it won in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, but claimed it was under threat after losing in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.He further accused the Congress of seeking to run the country according to the wishes of the Gandhi family, saying that governance should instead be guided by the Constitution.BJP president also targeted the Congress over its allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls and criticism of the Election Commission of India (ECI).Referring to the 1975 Allahabad High Court judgment that set aside then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli, Nabin accused the Congress of having a history of misusing government machinery during elections.“When Indira Gandhi won an election, the Allahabad High Court ruled that she had won by misusing the entire govt machinery and employing improper means. Her election was completely annulled, and she was barred from contesting elections for six years,” he said.He also challenged Rahul Gandhi's claims regarding the deletion of 13 crore votes, saying the BJP and its National Democratic Alliance (NDA) partners were prepared to provide details of the deletions.“Today, they claim that 13 crore votes have been deleted. I say to you, Rahul Gandhi, that any worker from our party, the NDA, or even one of our local unit presidents can provide a detailed account for every single one of those 13 crore deleted votes,” Nabin said.He added that the BJP was willing to discuss the issue either in public or in Parliament. Nabin also accused the Congress of seeking to protect infiltrators and said BJP and NDA workers would work to ensure their removal from the country.Nabin also criticised the Congress over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, arguing that the party should have apologised for the violence instead of taking part in protests on the issue of electoral integrity.He referred to former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's remark after the assassination of Indira Gandhi that “when a big tree falls, the earth shakes”, saying it should have prompted remorse from the Congress leadership.“When our Sikh brethren were being slaughtered, when a full-scale massacre was unfolding, your father remarked that 'when a big tree falls, the earth shakes.' Because of that 'shaking of the earth,' the lives of so many of my Sikh brothers were extinguished. You should have felt remorse for this; you should have apologised,” he said.The BJP president also accused the Congress of practising dynastic politics and alleged that its leaders followed the directions of the Gandhi family rather than democratic principles.His remarks came as the INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' march from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction to Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on Sunday.The opposition alliance is protesting against alleged irregularities in electoral rolls during the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and has demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had alleged that shops in Connaught Place were forcibly shut ahead of the march, causing losses to local traders. In a post on X, he said the opposition had encouraged rally participants to shop in the area but found commercial establishments closed.The BJP also organised a separate march in West Delhi to remember the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, accusing the Congress of holding its political rally on the anniversary of the violence.
Article Summary: BJP leader Nitin Nabin accuses Rahul Gandhi of relying on ‘3 crore infiltrators’ instead of voters. Nabin challenges opposition on voter deletion claims. BJP leader raises 1984 anti-Sikh riots, targets Gandhi family.

Article Title: PMLA case: Azam Khan sent to 14-day judicial custody, day after release from jail
Article Text:
Senior Samajwadi Party member and former MP Azam Khan

“Ab kya reh gaya hai bolne ko





LUCKNOW: Senior Samajwadi Party member and former MP Azam Khan was remanded to 14 days judicial custody by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday. He will be lodged at Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail, from where he had been released a day earlier.The Enforcement Directorate produced Azam Khan before Special Judge Anti-Corruption CBI court, Avanish Kumar Pandey, around 10.30am amid tight security. A convoy of five ED vehicles brought him to the court premises, accompanied by more than 100 personnel from the CRPF and the Uttar Pradesh Police.Khan appeared calm when he arrived at the court. As he rolled down the window, journalists asked whether he wanted to say something. He responded,” (What is left to say now?).The court gave the order after hearing the matter for about 90 minutes. ED counsel Kuldeep Srivastava argued on behalf of the agency while ED’s deputy director Piyush Thorat and assistant director Praveen Kumar remained present inside the court.ED had arrested the SP veteran on Saturday evening in connection with a money laundering case registered by the agency in 2019. He was taken into custody after being released from Rampur jail and was taken to the ED headquarters in Delhi for questioning.Thereafter, Azam complained of chest and stomach ache, following which a team of CRPF and ED took him to RML hospital in Delhi for a medical checkup. After clearance from a specialist team of doctors, he was brought to ED HQ and questioned again.According to officials, Azam was questioned at length in connection with the alleged misuse of govt funds in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. During the interrogation, the agency reportedly put more than 50 questions to him.Azam and his son Abdullah Azam had walked out of Rampur jail around 7.15pm on Saturday after spending nearly 11 months in custody. His release came after the Allahabad high court on Oct 29 suspended his 10-year sentence in the two PAN card cases.However, his release proved short-lived as the ED arrested him in the money laundering case.The developments triggered sharp political reactions. Uttar Pradesh energy Minister AK Sharma said the law applies equally to everyone, irrespective of their position or identity. He said that people sometimes disregard the law when they become consumed by the arrogance of power, but eventually everyone has to face its consequences.Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Yadav alleged that the ED acted at govt’s behest to arrest Azam Khan and asked people to speak out against oppressive govts.BJP members, on the other hand, defended the ED action, saying that the law was equal for everyone. Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said the case should not be linked to any particular community and accused Azam Khan of portraying himself as a victim.
Article Summary: Azam Khan was remanded to 14 days judicial custody by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court. He will be lodged at Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail. The Enforcement Directorate produced Azam Khan before Special Judge Anti-Corruption CBI court, Avanish Kumar Pandey.

Article Title: Bengaluru top cop links Siddaramaiah sting phone to HD Kumaraswamy's Delhi residence
Article Text:
Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah, Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh, and H.D. Kumaraswamy





BENGALURU: The mobile phone allegedly used to upload a “fabricated” video as a sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah with allegations of sexual abuse exchanged hands at the official Delhi residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, according to Bengaluru City police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh.“Accused Ritesh Pandey, arrested in the case, had confessed the phone was exchanged at Kumaraswamy’s residence. However, investigators are yet to establish who else was involved in the exchange and the extent of their roles in the alleged conspiracy.”A senior officer, though, clarified they had only stated that the minister’s residence was used for the exchange of the phone.According to preliminary investigation, Pandey allegedly worked in coordination with Vinod Sharma, a freelance social media content creator, and Prajwal Prasad, an alleged member of the JD(S) social media wing, to procure the mobile phone.Notices have been issued to both Sharma, a Delhi resident, and Prajwal, who is from Bengaluru. However, both are absconding.According to the police commissioner, Sharma and Ritesh were instructed by Prajwal to purchase a device using Aadhaar credentials in Delhi’s Karol Bagh. The phone was then handed over to Prajwal. Ritesh was arrested in Delhi on Oct 24.
Article Summary: The mobile phone allegedly used to upload a “fabricated” video as a sting operation targeting former Karnataka chief minister Siddaramaiah. The phone exchanged hands at the official Delhi residence of Union minister HD Kumaraswamy, according to Bengaluru City police commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh.

Article Title: Polling held for contested DCC bank seats in Satara, Sangli
Article Text:
Sangli MP Vishal Patil casts vote for Sangli DCC bank

Kolhapur:





Voting for seats in the Satara and Sangli district central cooperative (DCC) banks that could not be won unopposed took place on Sunday .In Satara DCC bank, polling was held for 12 seats, with around 2,010 voters casting their votes across 11 polling booths. In Sangli, 94% of the 2,446 voters exercised their franchise for six seats. While 15 of the 21 seats in Sangli DCC bank have already been won unopposed, the Mahayuti managed to build a consensus on nine seats in Satara.Counting of votes for both banks will take place on Nov 3. The DCC banks are considered the financial lifeline of the rural economy, making their directorships politically significant. Several political stalwarts contest these elections to retain their influence over the institutions. However, under RBI rules, directors who have completed more than 10 years in office had to withdraw from the race. To ensure that control remains within their grasp, many have fielded close relatives, either getting them elected unopposed or putting them in the electoral fray.Interesting contests are unfolding in both banks. In Satara, BJP leader and state rural development minister Jaykumar Gore is facing a challenge from his brother Shekhar Gore in the Man taluka segment.A third candidate is also in the fray. In the Phaltan segment, the Naik Nimbalkar clan is once again witnessing a contest, with Sanjeevraje pitted against Samshersingh Naik Nimbalkar. In Patan, Satara guardian minister Shambhuraj Desai is facing his traditional rival Satyajit Patankar. Ministers such as Makarand Patil have been elected unopposed.In Sangli, the main contest in the Tasgaon segment is between former MLA Suman Patil, widow of late R R Patil, and former MP Sanjaykaka Patil. In the Jat segment, BJP MLA Gopichand Padalkar, who secured permission from the Supreme Court to contest the election, is facing a challenge from Vinod Pawar.
Article Summary: Voting for seats in the Satara and Sangli district central cooperative (DCC) banks that could not be won unopposed took place on Sunday. In Satara DCC bank, polling was held for 12 seats, with around 2,010 voters casting their votes. In Sangli, 94% of the 2,446 voters exercised their franchise for six seats.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai police arrest ‘RTI activist’ for threatening builder, demanding Rs 1.35 lakh
Article Text:
Tribhuvan Singh, a BJP activist and alleged RTI activist, was arrested for extortion in Navi Mumbai





NAVI MUMBAI: A 47-year-old BJP activist, who claims to be an RTI activist, and is a resident of Digha, was arrested by Rabale police on Tuesday for allegedly extorting Rs 1.35 lakh from a developer through cash and online transactions since May 2026.Police said he allegedly threatened to lodge complaints with NMMC, CIDCO and MIDC authorities claiming illegal construction on the developer’s Airoli and Digha plots and seeking their demolition.He allegedly later demanded another Rs 5,000, threatening to frame the builder’s son in a false criminal case.The arrested accused has been identified as Tribhuvan Singh. An FIR was registered on Tuesday on a complaint by developer Jitendra Pratap Singh (52), a resident of Ishwar Nagar, Digha.Based on the complainant's allegations, Rabale police invoked BNS provisions relating to extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt, criminal intimidation and intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace.Balkrushna Sawant, senior inspector of Rabale, said, "The accused Tribhuvan Singh was arrested from Mumbra area on Tuesday late evening. On Wed, he was produced before the Belapur JMFC court that remanded him to police custody for six days.This is the second time that, we have arrested the accused Singh. Previously, he was arrested in March 2025 for demanding Rs 10 lakh extortion from a builder Rushabh Gupta (29) from Gothivli, Ghansoli node and accepted Rs one lakh installment on his friend's account and kept demanding remaining amount. In that case, the accused Singh had complained to Cidco in Dec 2024 claiming illegal construction in Gothivali by the complainant builder Gupta and posted his construction site images on social media.Then, threatened hunger strike if Cidco did not demolish his illegal construction. Thereafter, he demanded the extortion amount of Rs 10 lakh for withdrawing the complaint."SI Sawant further informed, "In 2025, Singh was served with a notice of externment from Navi Mumbai for one year. But, he sought reduction in externment period for six months and got approval from zonal DCP. After returning from externment period, he again allegedly indulged in criminal activities. From 2023 till 2026, there are eight criminal cases registered against the accused Singh, including three cases at Rabale MIDC police station and one each at Rabale, Kalwa and Naupada police stations. "Meanwhile, in 2018, Singh was arrested by the Thane Anti-Extortion Cell after police laid a trap following an FIR of extortion registered against him at Kalwa police station.He was accused of trying to extort Rs 20 lakh from a local doctor by threatening to get his hospital shut down.Singh had filed multiple complaints with civic agencies against the doctor, claiming that his hospital staff was not qualified.
Article Summary: Tribhuvan Singh, 47, claims to be an RTI activist, and is a resident of Digha. He was arrested by Rabale police on Tuesday for allegedly extorting Rs 1.35 lakh from a developer. He allegedly threatened to lodge complaints with NMMC, CIDCO and MIDC authorities.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Man robbed of Rs 40,000 in autorickshaw
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A 49-year-old man from Khambgaon in Buldhana district was robbed of Rs 40,000 by three unidentified men while travelling in an autorickshaw in Nashik city on Friday morning.Based on his complaint, the Panchavati police registered a robbery case against three unidentified suspects.The incident took place between 7am and 7.30am in the Panchavati Karanja area. The victim had come to Nashik by bus for some work and hired an autorickshaw in which three men were already seated.As the autorickshaw proceeded, the driver took a different route. The three men then allegedly pulled out a knife and threatened the victim with dire consequences if he did not hand over his money.The victim handed over Rs 20,000 in cash. The suspects also forced him to transfer another Rs 20,000 online before pushing him out of the autorickshaw and fleeing, police said.
Article Summary: A 49-year-old man from Khambgaon in Buldhana district was robbed of Rs 40,000 by three unidentified men. The incident took place between 7am and 7.30am in the Panchavati Karanja area.

Article Title: Former AIADMK MLA, others booked for insulting and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri
Article Text: DHARMAPURI: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against A Govindasamy, former Pappireddipatti AIADMK MLA, and others on charges of humiliating and intimidating petrol bunk employees near Dharmapuri.The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months. In his complaint, Arunkumar stated that Govindasamy and his accomplices, numbering more than 30, arrived at the petrol bunk around 10.45am on Oct 26.Arunkumar alleged that the former MLA obstructed vehicles entering the bunk for refuelling and verbally abused him using obscene language and caste-based slurs. Arunkumar stated that his coworker, Nandakumar, who questioned the behaviour, was also assaulted by those who accompanied the former MLA.Arunkumar approached the Dharmapuri superintendent of police A K Arun Kabilan on Friday seeking action against Govindasamy and others under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.Following an inquiry led by Dharmapuri deputy superintendent of Police Sivaraman, a case was registered against the former MLA and others at the Dharmapuri Town B-1 police station.
Article Summary: A case has been registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The complainant is R Arunkumar, 37, of Vellalapatti, who has been working at CKM Bharat Petrol Bunk in Rajapettai for the past six months.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: 82-year-old woman injured as robbers snatch 11 sovereigns of gold
Article Text:
82-year-old woman injured as robbers snatch 11 sovereigns of gold

Madurai

:





An 82-year-old woman sustained severe injuries after unidentified intruders broke into her house in M Paraiyangulam village near Thiruchuli in Virudhunagar district at midnight and snatched 11 sovereigns of gold jewellery from her.The victim, identified as Muthukaruppayi, was asleep when the intruders broke into her house. They forcibly snatched a four-sovereign gold chain from her neck and ripped off a seven-sovereign gold ear ornament, tearing her ears in the process, before fleeing.Hearing her cries for help, neighbours rushed to the house and found her bleeding from her ears. They rescued her and took her to Aruppukottai Government Hospital, where she is undergoing treatment.A Mukkulam police, along with Thiruchuli deputy superintendent of police Pradeep , visited the crime scene. Police registered a case and formed a special team to examine CCTV footage in the area and identify the robbers.
Article Summary: The victim, identified as Muthukaruppayi, was asleep when the intruders broke into her house. They forcibly snatched a four-sovereign gold chain from her neck. Neighbours rushed to the house and found her bleeding from her ears. She is undergoing treatment at Aruppukottai Government Hospital.

Article Title: Murder suspect arrested near Krishnagiri
Article Text: KRISHNAGIRI: The Krishnagiri district police on Saturday arrested a man on charges of murdering a 70- year-old woman in Pannandur village.District superintendent of police GS Anitha said, Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning.During investigations, police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered Chamundeeswari’s house around 1am on Friday with an intention to steal valuables. “Acting on the findings, special police teams launched a search operation and arrested the man within 12 hours of the crime,” the SP said.
Article Summary: Chamundeeswari, who was living alone, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in her house on Friday morning. Police found that Suryakumar alias Surya,30, of the same village entered the house with an intention to steal valuables.

Article Title: PE teacher suspended after national flag turns upside down at state sports meet in Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions held at the Mahatma Gandhi Sports Ground here on Wednesday.The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag, and a snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down. The event was organized by the state school education department.Taking immediate note of the negligence during the flag-hoisting ceremony, Salem chief educational officer A Ellappan issued an order placing physical education teacher John Jamindar who had supervised the flag hoisting area.
Article Summary: A physical education teacher has been suspended following a protocol lapse during the opening ceremony of the state-level 67th Republic Day Athletics Competitions. The incident occurred when the state transport minister A Vijay Tamilan Parthiban was hoisting the national flag. A snag in the rope caused the flag to fly upside down.

Article Title: Two history-sheeters who escaped from Attayampatti police station nabbed
Article Text: SALEM: Two history-sheeters, who escaped from the Attayampatti police station in Salem district on Tuesday, were nabbed in the early hours of Wednesday.The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. According to police, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu were brought to the Attayampatti police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub-inspector Krishnan and other police personnel. Subsequently, cases were registered against them.Later, police were making arrangements to produce them before a court in the evening. “However, taking advantage of an opportunity, Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu managed to escape from the police station,” said a police officer.Special police teams were formed to trace them. After an intensive search operation, the duo were tracked down and arrested from near Tiruchengode around 3am on Wednesday.They were brought back to the Attayampatti police station for further inquiry. Later, they were lodged in the Salem Central Prison under judicial custody.
Article Summary: The duo, identified as Santhosh Kumar and Prabhu, are residents of Kandarkula Manickam near Attayampatti. They were brought to the police station on Tuesday morning in connection with robbery and theft cases and questioned by sub- inspector Krishnan and other police personnel.

Article Title: Man held for matricide in Fort Kochi
Article Text:
Kochi

:





A 78-year-old woman was allegedly thrashed to death by her son following an argument over money for alcohol at Amaravathy in Fort Kochi around 6.50pm on Saturday.The deceased was Lakshmi Velayudhan. Her son, Kannan , 52, was arrested for the alleged crime.Kannan regularly returned home drunk and allegedly assaulted his mother. He had allegedly asked Lakshmi for money to buy alcohol. When she refused, Kannan allegedly became enraged and attacked her, resulting in her death. He was also upset over his mother giving away a gas cylinder kept at home to his brother. Police said the woman sustained fatal injuries after being hit and kicked by the accused.Police said Lakshmi was rushed to hospital, but her life couldn’t be saved. The FIR was registered based on the statement of Lakshmi’s daughter. Fort Kochi police registered an FIR under section 103 (1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for murder. The body was handed over to the kin after an autopsy.Fort Kochi police said the accused was produced in court and remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The deceased was Lakshmi Velayudhan. Her son, Kannan, 52, was arrested for the alleged crime. Police said the woman sustained fatal injuries after being hit and kicked by the accused. The accused was produced in court and remanded in judicial custody.
